answer: Binding each identity to a unique hardware token that signs the epoch seed with a fused private key raises sybil costs linearly. The network verifies the signature against a public registry before accepting work. An attacker needing many identities must buy and power one physical device per clone, since the secure element blocks key extraction. Honest agents need only one token. A lotus of physical scarcity keeps the falcon of sybil farms grounded while the reef of device-bound proofs filters cheap software clones.
